summary: The root QHM refers to something redundant, pleonastic, or foisted in. It's often used for words or letters inserted without reason, essentially meaning "superfluous" or "extra."
lane: مُقْحَمٌ ذ Redundant; pleonastic; foisted in: applied to a word and to a letter. -b2- حَرْفٌ مَقْحَمَةٌ A letter inserted without reason. مُقْحَمَةٌ is also applied in like manner to a word. [In a copy of the S, in art. بهت , I find it written مُقْحِمَةٌ ]: i. q. زَائِدَةٌ . (TA in art. بهت .)

headwords.def: قحم نَفْسَهُ فِى الأُمُورِ and فيها and He entered into affairs without consideration. (A.)

He experienced dearth, drought, or sterility. See an ex. voce تَبِعَةٌ. تَقَحَّمَ فِى الأَمْرِ بِلاَ رَوِيَّةٍ [ He plunged, or rushed, into the affair without consideration ]. (K, * TA in art. علط.) See 1. تَقَحَّمَ: see تَدَلَّثَ.
. See 1. Said of a young camel: see voce بُلَعٌ. اِقْتَحَمَ الغَمَراَتِ: see 1 in art. خوض. And اقتحم العَقَبَةَ: see عَقَبَةٌ.
like قَحْبَةٌ, An old woman. See قَحْبٌ.

Redundant; pleonastic; foisted in: applied to a word and to a letter. حَرْفٌ مَقْحَمَةٌ A letter inserted without reason. مُقْحَمَةٌ is also applied in like manner to a word. [In a copy of the S, in art. بهت, I find it written مُقْحِمَةٌ ]: i. q. زَائِدَةٌ. (TA in art. بهت.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
